content:
From some of the comments here, it can be seen that a small group of people strongly oppose all AI tools, including Apple Intelligence. This sentiment has given rise to an unofficial tool that allows users to disable this feature on Mac and delete all downloaded Siri AI models.

We mentioned yesterday that doing so may carry risks, but there are now opinions suggesting that Apple may ultimately need to officially support the option to remove AI, in order to protect hardware sales……

The backlash against generative AI in society continues to grow, with opponents citing a wide variety of reasons — some worry about the survival of humanity, while others simply do not want unwanted AI features taking up device storage space.

The latest Apple Intelligence models may require up to 14GB of storage space, which is a significant burden for 256GB models if you do not want these features. Hence independent developer Om Lahore has created a project called RemoveMacAI.

Top Liked Reply by GoldGrapes

"It's clearly only a minority speaking up," yet you say Apple needs to support removing AI to protect hardware sales? How would a minority affect hardware sales?

As we mentioned yesterday, using this tool is not without risk. Since Apple Intelligence is deeply embedded in macOS 27, it may have unforeseen effects on some basic functions.

However, some believe Apple may need to provide an official method to completely remove Apple Intelligence from Mac. John Gruber of Daring Fireball has pointed out that some organisations have already banned the installation of AI tools.

To clarify, Apple actually already provides a large number of control options for organisations using device management. Apple currently states that organisations can "restrict the use" of certain Apple Intelligence features, and there are individual toggles to enable or disable each feature separately. What is currently lacking is a master switch to disable all Apple Intelligence features at once and remove all downloaded models.

This is not yet an urgent issue, but as future Macs begin to drop support for older versions of macOS, Apple hardware sales may start to be affected if users are not given an easy way to remove AI models.
